(2) Petitioner's husband, who was
employed as a Group D employee in Union
Bank of India, died within four months of
his marriage. Learned Counsel for the
petitioner points out that the marriage
between petitioner and her husband was
solemnised on 14.4.2024, while death of
her husband occurred on 15.8.2024.
Petitioner applied for compassionate
appointment, however her request is not
being considered only on the ground that
she has not produced any certificate to
indicate that she is the legal heir. By means
of this writ petition, petitioner has sought
the following reliefs:
"1. Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus commanding and directing
the respondents to consider the candidature of the
petitioner for compassionate appointment as
dependent (Spouse) of Late Govind Raj.
2. Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding and directing
the respondent to consider the representation

UKHC010139882026
2026:UHC:7566
dated 10.7.2026 of the petitioner (annexed as
Annexure No. 10 to this writ petition, from page
no. 36 to page no. 37 of this writ petition) with
giving opportunity of hearing for petitioner for
consideration in terms of Modified Scheme, 2025
(annexed as Annexure No. 11 to this writ petition,
from page 38 to page 44 of this writ petition)."
(3) Learned Counsel for the petitioner
submits that petitioner's mother-in-law and
father-in-law have given No Objection
Certificate in favour of petitioner, regarding
compassionate appointment; petitioner has
survivorship certificate, issued by SDM,
Haridwar, which shows that she is legally
wedded wife of Govind Raj; she also has
ration card, in which she is shown as wife of
Govind Raj. He further submits that in the
death certificate of Govind Raj also,
petitioner's name is mentioned as wife of
deceased. He further submits that a child
was also born to the petitioner on
21.12.2024 and in the birth certificate also,
name of deceased is mentioned as father of
the child. Thus it is contended that there is
sufficient evidence available with petitioner
to prove her relationship with Govind Raj,
yet bank authorities are unnecessarily
harassing the petitioner.
(4) Since there is no rival claim made
by anyone in the family of petitioner's
husband, including her brother-in-law or
sister-in-law, and petitioner's case is
covered as per the policy applicable in the
bank regarding compassionate appointment
and only objection raised by the bank is
regarding legal heir certificate, therefore,
doubt raised by bank authorities on
petitioner's eligibility for compassionate
appointment appears to be unfounded. Writ
petition is, accordingly, disposed of with a

direction to the competent authority in the
bank to consider petitioner's claim for
compassionate appointment, based on the
documents available with her, and pass
appropriate order, granting compassionate
appointment to her, within two months from
the date of presentation of certified copy of
this order.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
